question: Should generic `tool-progress` metadata become a supported public plugin-SDK reply-payload contract, or remain an internal host-to-bundled-plugin signal?
rationale: The PR adds a public constant and predicate that third-party plugins could depend on; code inspection can identify the implementation defect but cannot determine the intended long-term SDK ownership.

options.title: Approve the public contract
options.body: Keep the generic SDK metadata, document its narrow transient-progress semantics, and fix all Slack rendering paths before merge.

options.title: Keep the signal internal
options.body: Replace the public exports with a narrow internal or bundled-plugin seam while retaining producer-owned typing.

options.title: Pause the PR
options.body: Defer the change until maintainers choose a broader cross-channel progress presentation contract.

recommendation.title: Approve the public contract
recommendation.body: Keep the generic SDK metadata, document its narrow transient-progress semantics, and fix all Slack rendering paths before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person to both the Slack structured-delivery implementation and the public SDK baseline containing the proposed contract.
